verdict: THE LEGIBILITY LAW PREDICTS SAE MONOSEMANTICITY (a new bridge to mech-interp). The SAME scalar property, stored two ways: the AMORTIZED code (a shared encoder infers it) is linearly legible (|r| 0.99) AND an SAE recovers it MONOSEMANTICALLY -- p decodes from just ~2 features (top-2 decode 0.95, the +/- pair). The FREE per-item code SCRAMBLES (linear |r| 0.46, info present nonlinearly 0.78) AND the SAE finds it only DISTRIBUTED -- top-2 features decode just 0.29 while the FULL feature set gives 0.71 (SUPERPOSITION). So amortization vs free storage is a CONTROLLABLE cause of superposition: a free code goes polysemantic, an amortized code stays monosemantic. Connects the legibility law to the SAE/superposition literature, completing script 09's free-code half (best single feature |r| 0.72).
